incidentDuringRound.what: The implementer idled mid-mutation with a live serializer mutation in src/core/canonical-json.ts - child 1's Layer-0 file, which five shape-(a) anchors route through.
incidentDuringRound.howItWasCaught: It had LABELLED the mutation in place with what it was and that it must be reverted. That label is the only reason the LEAD could tell in one look that this was an in-flight proof rather than someone actually changing the serializer. A silent mutate-and-restore habit would have left an unexplained edit to a Layer-0 file, indistinguishable from a real change.
incidentDuringRound.whatTheImplementerDidRight: It killed the in-flight background suite run BEFORE reverting, rather than letting it finish against a mutated file. That run would have produced a clean-looking result measured against a deliberately broken serializer - a false green that outlives the mutation.
incidentDuringRound.leadResponse: Froze all gate activity and committed nothing until the revert was independently verified by hash and by an empty `git diff HEAD -- src/`.
incidentDuringRound.standingRule: Never leave a mutation live across a background wait. Either run the proof in the foreground so the window closes when the run does, or revert first and re-mutate when ready to watch it. The window is the risk, not the mutation. And always label a mutation in place - it is what makes an incident diagnosable.
